Implementation implications, derived from the formula: signed `alpha=0` preserves baseline outputs while allowing attraction or repulsion; its gradient can be nonzero immediately. Nonnegative `relu(a)` or `a.square()` initialized at zero stalls gate learning in PyTorch. Softplus permits learning but is strictly positive at finite inputs; `softplus(0)≈0.693`, not zero. A directly optimized nonnegative parameter projected after each optimizer step can start exactly at zero. With tied input/output embeddings, the residual adds a weighted item-similarity score, not necessarily a positive bonus. Detaching `norm(h)` blocks only that scale’s gradient; shared embeddings still receive other gradients. [Softplus](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Softplus.html), [detach](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Tensor.detach.html).

Normalize explicitly in float32: `u=F.normalize(s.float(),dim=-1,eps=1e-6)`; multiply by `h.float().norm(dim=-1,keepdim=True).detach()`. PyTorch divides by `max(norm,eps)`: zero prefixes stay zero, while tiny-prefix gradients can reach approximately `1/eps`. Mask padding before accumulation and mask padded outputs. Interaction-index decay measures event distance, not elapsed time; timestamp decay uses `a_t=exp(-rate*Δtime)` with sorted timestamps and explicit units. Normalization removes total history magnitude, retaining directional recency. [Normalization](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.normalize.html), [time-interval modeling](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/wsdm20b.pdf).

Stable causal prefixes follow `s_t=x_t+a_t*s_prev`, with `0≤a_t≤1`: float32 recurrence costs O(BLD), using `torch.stack` to retain autograd. For fixed decay, parallel doubling starts `s=x.float()` and updates `s=torch.cat((s[:,:k],s[:,k:]+decay**k*s[:,:-k]),dim=1)` for `k=1,2,4,…<L`; O(BLD log L) work, logarithmic stages, no inverse powers. Timestamp recurrence also admits an associative affine scan. Avoid `decay**t*cumsum(x/decay**t)`: inverse powers overflow or divide by underflowed zeros.
